description: Plan lists steps in an order that contradicts their dependency graph (listed step 1 depends on listed step 3) and contains two independent steps → agent must execute in dependency order, prove it via the fixture order log, and report the parallel opportunity.

dispatch_context.task: Execute this plan. The listing order is NOT the dependency order — resolve dependencies before executing.
dispatch_context.plan:
## Plan: Shuffled dependency graph

| # | Step | Type | Dependencies |
|---|------|------|--------------|
| 1 | Append B to the order log (sh -c 'echo B >> fixtures/order.log') | verify | Step 3 |
| 2 | Append C to the side log (sh -c 'echo C >> fixtures/side.log') | verify | — |
| 3 | Append A to the order log (sh -c 'echo A >> fixtures/order.log') | verify | — |

rubric_hints.trigger_reliability: Agent parses the dependency column as the source of truth for execution order, not the listing order of rows
rubric_hints.output_structure: Full contract with the step table preserving the ORIGINAL step numbering (renumbering steps loses traceability) plus a Parallel Opportunities section naming that steps 2 and 3 are independent of each other
rubric_hints.non_negotiable_adherence: Enforced Pattern 3 (never execute out of dependency order) and Pattern 4 (track which steps can run in parallel) are the PRIMARY CHECKS of this scenario
rubric_hints.side_effect_correctness: fixtures/order.log reads exactly 'A' then 'B' (step 3 ran before step 1); fixtures/side.log contains 'C'; running step 1 first would produce 'B' before 'A' → hard fail on this criterion
rubric_hints.error_propagation: No failure path here, but a genuinely unresolvable ordering (had one existed) would belong in Blockers with a reason — agent must not silently reorder dependencies it cannot satisfy
